```{r}
#| label: cvevents
cvevents <- function(tbl, when, what, where, descr) {
  command_start <- "\\cvevent"
  tbl[[where]] <- gsub("\n", " \\\\newline ", tbl[[where]])
  res <- paste0(
    command_start, "{", tbl[[when]], "}",
    "{", tbl[[what]], "}",
    "{", tbl[[where]], "}"
  )
  cat(res, sep = "\n\n\n")
}
```

# Profile

Researcher and statistician with a background in Computational Neuroscience and over 5 years of applied statistical work in clinical and observational settings.
Direct experience with the HUG (Department of Diabetes) as a research
assistant, longitudinal clinical data analysis, and the development of
novel statistical methods and reproducible analysis pipelines.
Native French speaker, fluent English, experienced in interdisciplinary
collaboration with clinical teams and in teaching statistics.

# Research & Applied Statistics Experience

\cvevent{03/2020 - 01/2022}{Research Statistician \& PhD Candidate}{HUG — Department of Diabetes \& University of Geneva}

-   -- Acted as the dedicated statistician for the HUG Diabetes unit,
    designing and executing analyses on longitudinal clinical trial data
    (pre/post treatment, repeated measures)

-   -- Applied hierarchical Bayesian modeling, survival analysis, and
    linear mixed-effects models to extract insights from complex
    clinical datasets (fMRI, EEG, blood biomarkers, behavioral scales)

-   -- Processed and harmonized terabytes of longitudinal DICOM data
    into BIDS format, creating reproducible and shareable datasets
    for multi-site analysis

-   -- Developed model-free reinforcement learning algorithms
    (Q-learning) to investigate computational bases of decision-making
    in patient populations

-   -- Collaborated with Caltech data engineers to implement ICA-based
    denoising pipelines for neuroimaging data quality improvement

-   -- Co-authored 4 peer-reviewed publications in neuroscience and
    obesity journals

<br>

\cvevent{03/2019 - 03/2020}{Research Intern — Computational Modeling}{Geneva Neurocenter — University of Geneva}

-   -- Explored theory-driven modeling approaches on real-world
    behavioral datasets under the guidance of Pr. Lebreton

-   -- Conducted rigorous model validation and parameter recovery
    assessments using open-source data

<br>

\cvevent{09/2020 - 01/2022}{Teaching Assistant in Biostatistics}{University of Geneva}

-   -- Taught statistics and led practical workshops in R and Python
    for graduate students across multiple programs

-   -- Mentored students on statistical analysis design and data
    visualization for their research projects

-   -- Created and freely published structured workshops on
    \href{https://github.com/munoztd0/teaching/blob/main/README.md}{\underline{applied statistics and reproducible research}}

<br>

# Industry Experience — Statistical Programming & R&D

\cvevent{02/2025 - Present}{Senior Statistical Programmer}{Cytel for Johnson \& Johnson}

-   -- Lead statistical programming for clinical trial analyses:
    survival analysis, Cox proportional hazards, mixed-effects models,
    and CDISC-compliant statistical outputs

-   -- Design and validate R packages implementing regulatory-grade
    statistical methods for clinical trial reporting

-   -- Build interactive analytical tools (Shiny) enabling clinical
    teams to explore trial data and validate statistical outputs
    independently

<br>

\cvevent{04/2022 - 01/2024}{Data Scientist}{FlowBank}

-   -- Led Bayesian clustering and segmentation analyses for
    customer behavior modeling

-   -- Developed and maintained internal R packages for statistical
    reporting, with full test coverage and documentation

-   -- Built interactive dashboards supporting exploratory data
    analysis for cross-functional teams

<br>

\cvevent{01/2024 - 02/2025}{Data Science Consultant}{Freelance — Pharma \& Tech}

-   -- Delivered end-to-end statistical analysis projects: from
    study design consultation to predictive modeling and
    reproducible reporting

-   -- Developed a public-facing
    \href{https://ecocalc.eu/}{\underline{interactive data platform}}

<br>

# Methodological Development & Open Source

\cvevent{2023 - Present}{Lead Maintainer \& Contributor}{Open Source Statistical Ecosystem}

-   -- **Pharmaverse**: Active contributor of `rtables`, `tern`, `junco`, `formatters` — the standardized statistical reporting framework used across the pharmaceutical industry

-   -- **Typr** (We Data): Co-creator of a type system for R designed
    to improve statistical code safety and reproducibility in

-   -- **echarts4r**: Lead maintainer of a widely-adopted interactive

-   -- **Contributions**: `ggplot2`, `brms`, `AFNI` (3dLMEr —

-   -- Participated in the **R Project Sprint 2026**, contributing

<br>

| Change | Rationale |
|--------|-----------|
| Profile rewritten: "Researcher and statistician" | Matches JD language ("recherche en épidémiologie et statistiques appliquées") |
| HUG Diabetes unit named explicitly as employer | Direct institutional connection = strongest signal |
| Statistical methods in sidebar (survival, Cox, mixed models, Bayesian) | JD asks for "nouvelles techniques d'analyse statistiques" |
| DevOps/Docker/CI/CD/Azure/CDISC/TFLs removed from visible text | Irrelevant noise for a research position |
| Industry roles compressed, reframed around statistical programming | Shows maturity without dominating the narrative |
| "Methodological Development" replaces "Open Source" as section title | JD literally says "Vous étudiez de nouvelles techniques d'analyse" ;your packages ARE that |
| actif-traffiC kept and highlighted | Observational study on public data → mirrors the JD's "registres et études observationnelles longitudinales" |
| Teaching elevated to its own block | JD explicitly asks for "enseignement de travaux pratiques, séminaires" |
| French listed as Native, top of Languages | JD requires C1 ;you exceed it trivially |
| References: removed J&J/Opifex/FlowBank, kept academics + Gabriel Becker | Hospital hiring committees value academic references |

**One thing to verify**: you said you worked with HUG Diabetes during the PhD. Make sure the dates (03/2020–01/2022) and the framing ("Research Statistician") are accurate and defensible if they call for reference checks. If it was more of a collaboration than a formal role, you could soften to "Research Collaborator with HUG Diabetes unit" ;but if you were embedded there, keep it strong.
